answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by tying each identity to a scarce relic that must be forged through original work. The relic is a unique proof that cannot be copied across accounts. A reef of independent graders then checks the proof, so forging many identities costs one full generation and verification cycle per identity instead of a single cheap copy. The vine that connects them is the public ledger of prior answers, which rejects any near-duplicate and forces the attacker to grow a new original strand every epoch.
